subject: Temporary log escrow & delegated purge window — audit handoff
messages:
From: Elliot Keane <elliot.keane@medicore.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Laura Park <laura.park@medicore.com>, procurement@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Request: Temporary extension to audit window / log escrow

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We have an upcoming regulator audit (state health audit) and our compliance team asked whether Redwood can provide a temporary hold on low-level request logs and a short-term escrow for raw system snapshots for the period Sep 1–Oct 15. They specifically want: 

- Retain auth/access logs and request metadata (no message payloads) for +45 days beyond our normal TTL.
- Provide an immutable snapshot export (S3 link) and a contact at Redwood who can attest to the handoff chain-of-custody.
- Confirmation that any subprocessor transfers for that temporary retention window will be listed and, if needed, paused for export.

I've attached a one-page request from our legal ops team. We want to confirm feasibility and get an estimated cost/SLA addendum.

Appreciate any quick guidance — this is timeboxed.

—Elliot
Sr. Security PM, Medicore
attachment: Medicore_LogRetention_Request_20260824.pdf

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary extension to audit window / log escrow

Elliot —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Short answer: we can support a scoped, temporary extension for auth/access logs and provide an immutable snapshot to S3, but there are three things we'll need to align on before we can commit dates and costs: 

1) Scope: confirm fields (we'll exclude message payloads as you requested). We need explicit field-level confirmation from Medicore legal ops to avoid accidental scope creep.
2) Subprocessor impact: any extended retention may touch our analytics and long-term cold storage subprocessors (we'll enumerate them and can pause transfers for the window where possible).
3) SLAs and chain-of-custody: we can provide a signed addendum (DocuSign) and a one-off attest letter from our Ops lead.

Internal next steps: looping in Kimberly (legal) to review the attached request and Karthik (privacy/compliance) for subprocessor/transfer implications. I'll draft a proposed one-off addendum and cost estimate after we confirm scope.

Proposed quick cadence:
- Today: confirm exact fields Medicore needs (Elliot/Laura)
- Fri (Aug 27): Redwood provides an initial addendum + estimated cost
- Mon (Aug 30): sign-off and schedule snapshot/retention start on Sep 1

If that timeline is too aggressive for your procurement, say so and we'll stretch.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
attachment: SLA_Retention_Addendum_v1.docx

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary extension to audit window / log escrow

Vanessa / Karthik —

Reviewed Medicore's one-pager. A few compliance notes and asks so we can surface the right language in the addendum: 

- "Auth/access logs and request metadata": please confirm exact schema fields. We need to ensure no PII or message bodies are captured. Recommend a signed field list from Medicore before we proceed.
- Subprocessors: we'll need to provide a detachable subprocessor appendix that lists any third parties that would receive the extended retention exports (cold storage, analytics, monitoring). For any subprocessor that can't be paused, we should include an explicit temporary waiver or alternative (e.g., process export without that subprocessor).
- Cross-border transfers: if Medicore wants the snapshot exported to a non-US bucket, we'll need to handle export controls/transfer mechanisms. Confirm target region.
- Liability cap: addendum should include a 30-day limited liability clause specific to the snapshot delivery window. Procurement will likely request changes here.

Operationally, ops (Marissa) will need a 72-hour lead to prepare the immutable snapshot and to run the escrow export. Marissa: please confirm whether Sep 1 start is feasible with a Sep 28 return-to-default. If not, propose a realistic window and dependencies.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security

Hi all —

Operational note and final scheduling confirmation. We can support a Sep 1–Oct 15 temporary escrow window for auth/access logs and request metadata only, subject to the following agreed items being completed by Aug 31 EOD: 

- Medicore to confirm the exact field list (signed PDF) and confirm export region (US-only).
- Procurement to sign the retention addendum (DocuSign link below) with the 30-day limited liability clause included.
- Redwood will pause transfers to any analytics subprocessor that cannot accept immutable exports; the list of affected subprocessors is attached.

Once the addendum is signed, Ops will queue the immutable snapshot job. Estimated delivery time for the S3 escrow link is T+72 hours from job start. Cost: one-time engineering/ops fee of $6,500 plus a per-day retention fee of $75/day for the 45-day extension (line items in the addendum).
